tagline: Explore the data. Understand the trends. Observe the Earth better.

meta.title: Terra Sense · Observing soil trends
meta.description: Terra Sense makes soil moisture and soil temperature trends readable, from NASA data (GLDAS, MODIS).

hero.badge: NASA Space Apps Challenge · Soil Trend Detective
hero.lead: Soil moisture shapes crops, vegetation and the water available to us. NASA Earth observation data keeps track of it month after month. Terra Sense helps you read these changes and check whether they are real.

problem.title: What happens when the soil loses its balance?
problem.lead: Soil moisture is not an isolated measurement. It links rainfall, vegetation, crops and the water that seeps deeper. When it changes over time, these systems change with it.

items.title: Weakened farmland
items.text: Less water in the top few centimetres means earlier stress for seedlings and higher irrigation needs. Productivity depends directly on this reserve.

items.title: Ecosystems under pressure
items.text: Vegetation, wetlands and livestock depend on available water. A harsher dry season reduces plant cover and watering points.

items.title: Invisible but essential water
items.text: Part of the soil's water seeps down and recharges aquifers. Soil that stays drier for longer can reduce that recharge.
items.note: Note: soil moisture is not a measurement of groundwater. Terra Sense displays no groundwater data.

mission.titleStart: NASA provides the data. Terra Sense makes it
mission.lead: Turning observation into understanding: every result shown can be traced back to the dataset it comes from.

observe.title: Observe the Earth
observe.text: The series come from NASA Giovanni, which averages GLDAS Noah (soil) and MODIS (aerosol) products over the area. Years of monthly values make it possible to tell a season from a change.

datasets.what: Soil moisture and temperature, 0–10 and 10–40 cm

trends.title: Identify the trends
trends.text: The Mann-Kendall test tells whether a steady change is statistically supported or compatible with chance. The Theil-Sen slope estimates its size. Neither establishes a cause.

understand.title: Understand the results
understand.text: The assistant explains a trend, a p-value or a method, from the platform's own calculations. It is an interpretation tool: it cites its sources and says what it does not know.
understand.future: Coming later: model explanations with SHAP. No SHAP model is published today.

closing.title: Observe the Earth. Understand its changes.
closing.text: Pick a variable, move through the months, compare series and check every trend.

about.title: About Terra Sense
intro: Terra Sense is a platform for observing soil trends, developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge around the Soil Trend Detective concept.

It addresses a simple difficulty: Earth observation series exist, but they are hard to read and harder still to interpret. Terra Sense shows them on a globe, plots them over time and tests whether their changes are statistically supported.
For Yaoundé, you can explore soil moisture and soil temperature at two depths, evaporation, runoff and aerosols, month by month, and ask the assistant your questions.

sources.title: Data sources
sources.intro: Not every variable comes from the same product. Each series is tied to its original dataset.

items.name: NASA Giovanni
items.role: Computes monthly means over the 11.4–11.65 °E, 3.75–3.98 °N area and exports them as CSV.
items.limits: One value per month for the whole area: no spatial variation inside it.

items.name: GLDAS Noah 0.25° monthly, version 2.0
items.role: Soil moisture 0–10 and 10–40 cm, soil temperature 0–10 cm.
items.limits: Values computed by a land-surface model forced by observations. Version 2.0 ends in 2014.

items.name: GLDAS Noah 0.25° monthly, version 2.1
items.role: Evaporation, surface runoff, soil temperature 10–40 cm.
items.limits: Land-surface model; different forcing from version 2.0.

items.name: MODIS Aqua, level 3 monthly, collection 6.1
items.limits: Satellite measurement on a 1° grid; months without a measurement stay empty.

items.name: NASA Earthdata
items.role: Access portal and documentation for the GLDAS and MODIS products.

items.name: geoBoundaries
items.role: Outline of Yaoundé: union of the Yaoundé I to VII districts.
items.limits: Used for drawing only; values remain those of the Giovanni area.

items.name: Mann-Kendall
items.text: Compares each measurement with every later one to tell whether the series rises or falls consistently. For monthly series the platform uses the seasonal version (month by month) or the Hamed and Rao correction for autocorrelation. A trend is called significant when p < 0.05.

items.name: Theil-Sen
items.text: Median of the slopes between all pairs of measurements. It estimates the speed of change, per year or per decade, and resists extreme values.

items.name: SHAP
items.text: Future work. No predictive model or SHAP explanation is published today.

freshness.title: Data freshness
freshness.text: The catalogue does not provide an update date. Latest published observation: {end}.

items.label: Geographic coverage
items.text: One area: Yaoundé. The outline follows the seven districts; values are the Giovanni mean over the 11.4–11.65 °E, 3.75–3.98 °N rectangle.

items.label: Missing data
items.text: Months without a value stay empty in the charts. No value is interpolated or replaced with zero.

items.label: Resolution
items.text: GLDAS: 0.25°; MODIS: 1°. These cells are larger than the city: they describe a regional mean.

items.label: Observation, model, statistics
items.text: MODIS is a satellite measurement; GLDAS is a model estimate. Trends, slopes and p-values are derived results computed by the platform.
